claims.rationale: The printed-frame vibration complaint is a soft structural mode low enough to sit inside the flight controller's control loop: the gyro sees it, the PID loop amplifies it, the motors get hot. Betaflight's dynamic notch and gyro low-pass handle a resonance above ~200 Hz with little delay; below ~150 Hz filtering it costs control. Measured by a 2.5D plate FE of the generated layout, hub clamped at the FC posts, motor+prop as point masses (conservative: a free-flying hub moves and raises the mode). REVISED 2026-10-07 from 'arm cantilever frequency above hover motor rotation frequency': that estimate ignored the duct's own mass (it put the arm at 452 Hz; the FE with the ducts on it says ~190 Hz), and the criterion would have failed every commercial whoop frame, which fly well on RPM filtering.
claims.statement: The frame's first out-of-plane mode (duct pods bouncing on the arms) is at or above 200 Hz

params.name: motor_mass_g

params.name: motor_body_d
params.rationale: mm, envelope of the 1102 bell for the seat and clearance checks. The listing's '11 mm' is the stator; the bell is wider. ASSUMPTION until one is measured with calipers (claim A3 / P4).

params.name: motor_h
params.rationale: mm, 1102 (2026) base to shaft tip (listing).

params.name: motor_hole_circle_d
params.rationale: mm, 1102 mount: 3 x M1.4 on a 6.6 mm circle (vendor). Shared by most 08xx/10xx/11xx whoop motors, so the frame takes other motors later.

params.name: motor_screw_clear_d
params.rationale: mm, clearance for M1.4. 1.5 is the nominal free fit; FDM holes print about 0.1-0.2 mm small, and a screw that has to be forced through cracks a 1.8 mm seat.

params.name: motor_screw_len
params.rationale: mm, the M1.4 x 3 screws that come with the motors.

params.name: motor_centre_relief_d
params.rationale: mm, hole under the motor for the shaft end and its C-clip. Sized by the seat, not the clip: the screw holes' inner edges sit 2.45 mm from the centre, and 2.3 leaves a 1.3 mm web (3 beads, cad.wall_thickness). 3.5 lost: a 0.70 mm web. The clip's real size is part of A3 - if it does not clear, open the hole with a 3 mm drill and expect C7 to flag the thinner web.

params.name: motor_kv
params.rationale: rpm/V, the kit's 1102 21000KV (2026).

params.name: motor_thrust_max_g
params.rationale: g per motor, full throttle, 1S: BetaFPV's published test of the 1102 22000KV on a GF-1635 40 mm 3-blade. The 2026 21000KV has no published test; this sibling's 40 mm figure is used as a FLOOR for the kit's 45 mm props (a bigger disc on the same motor makes more static thrust).

params.name: motor_thrust_test_v
params.rationale: V of that thrust test. NOT STATED by the vendor - ASSUMPTION A6. If the test was at 3.7 V the real margin is ~30% better than modelled.

params.name: prop_d
params.rationale: mm, Gemfan 1811 3-blade, 1.5 mm shaft: the props that come in the kit. 40 mm lost: it needs a separate purchase and gives up disc area.

params.name: prop_mass_g
params.rationale: g per prop, GF 1811 (vendor).

params.name: prop_hub_drop
params.rationale: mm, prop plane below the motor's top: the hub presses down onto the shaft.

params.name: fc_mass_g
params.rationale: g, BetaFPV Matrix 1S 3-in-1 (FC + 12 A ESC + ELRS receiver), with its BT2.0 lead (vendor). No video transmitter: nothing to license or burn out.

params.name: fc_hole_spacing
params.rationale: mm, Matrix 1S 3IN1 square mounting pattern (vendor: 25.5 x 25.5).

params.name: fc_board_side
params.rationale: mm, PCB edge, square. ASSUMPTION A4: not published; whoop boards on a 25.5 pattern run 28-30 mm. Measure before printing.

params.name: fc_pcb_t
params.rationale: mm, AIO board thickness, for the screw stack.

params.name: fc_top_components_h

params.rationale: mm.

params.name: plate_t

params.name: arm_w
params.rationale: mm, arm width at plate level.

params.name: rib_w
params.rationale: mm, the stiffening rib along each arm: 3 beads of 0.42.

params.name: rib_h
params.rationale: mm above the plate. Stiffness goes as h^3, so this rib is most of the arm's bending stiffness; it stops below the motor seat so it never meets a prop.

params.name: spoke_w
params.rationale: mm, flat flange under each spoke's rib (5 beads). The rib carries the bending; 2.5 lost: 0.3 g for nothing the FE could see.

params.name: prop_tip_gap
params.rationale: mm, radial gap prop tip to duct wall. Under ~0.75 a 1 mm print error or a bent prop strikes; over ~2 the duct stops helping thrust.

rejected.why: inside one print error plus prop flex of a strike

params.name: duct_wall
params.rationale: mm, 3 beads at 0.42 mm: the fdm min-wall rule.

params.name: duct_above_prop
params.rationale: mm of duct above the prop plane: the lip that fingers and furniture meet before the tips. 3.0, 2.0 and 1.5 lost: 0.8, 0.5 and 0.25 g for no safety a kid would notice - the ring around the tips is the guard.

params.name: duct_lattice
params.rationale: Below the prop band the duct wall is a 45-degree diamond lattice. A solid wall made the ducts ~14 g, over half the frame (see PARAMS).

rejected.why: ~14 g of ducts: frame 20.5 g, thrust-to-weight 2.2
took 0.3 g out; not worth the print time
their tops are bridges/overhangs that need support

params.name: lattice_overhang_deg
params.rationale: Steepest lattice window edge, degrees from vertical: 5 under the 45 deg no-support rule, so slicer rounding never lands a face on the wrong side of it.

params.name: lattice_above_members
params.rationale: Start the lattice above the tallest member that joins the duct, instead of above the plate with solid patches where members join.

params.name: joint_margin
params.rationale: mm of solid duct wall kept either side of a spoke or web where it joins the duct (no window there). One strut width (1.3) lost: 0.9 g of extra wall.

params.name: lattice_margin
params.rationale: mm of solid wall between the plate's top face and the lattice (2 layers).

params.name: lattice_strut_w
params.rationale: mm, lattice strut width square to the strut: 3 beads, same rule as the wall.

params.name: duct_band_below_prop
params.rationale: mm of solid duct wall below the prop plane, where the tips run (the sweep is +-1.5 mm). 3.0 lost: 0.7 g, which put thrust-to-weight under 3.0 once the lattice's flat-ceiling half-cells were taken out.

params.name: foot_w
params.rationale: mm, flange at each duct's foot. Equal to the wall, i.e. no flange: a 5 mm brim does the bed-adhesion job and is snipped off; a flange stays and weighs.

params.name: web_h
params.rationale: mm, height of the wall joining neighbouring ducts. The cheapest stiffness in the frame: 4.0 -> 6.0 took the first mode from 213 to 283 Hz for 0.12 g, because the duct ring IS the structure in the spoked layout.

params.name: fc_yaw_deg
params.rationale: The AIO is mounted turned 45 degrees so its corners point between the ducts rather than into them; that is worth ~6 mm of wheelbase. Betaflight then needs board alignment yaw = 45 (build guide step, physical claim P3).

rejected.why: AIO corners point into the ducts; wheelbase grows ~6 mm to clear them

params.name: fc_post_od
params.rationale: mm, printed posts the AIO sits on. 3.6 lost: 1.25 mm of wall round the 1.1 mm pilot, under the 1.26 mm process minimum (cad.wall_thickness).

params.name: hub_t

params.rationale: mm, narrowest optimised member that gets printed (4 beads). params.name: hub_hole_margin

params.name: hub_margin
params.rationale: mm of plate around each FC post in the hub outline. 1.5 lost: 0.1 g the strap and the posts did not need.

params.name: fc_post_h
params.rationale: mm above the plate. The battery strap runs over the hub UNDER the AIO, so this is strap_t plus 3 mm for the AIO's bottom-side parts. 3.0 lost: it left 1.5 mm, and the strap would press on the ESC's FETs.

params.name: fc_pilot_d
params.rationale: mm, pilot for an M1.4 screw threading into PETG.

params.name: fc_screw_len
params.rationale: mm, M1.4 x 6 screws down through the AIO into the posts (claim C8).

params.name: fc_board_clear
params.rationale: mm minimum between the AIO's edge and any duct wall, in plan.

params.name: strap_t
params.rationale: mm, thickness of a hook-and-loop strap where it laps over the hub.

params.name: strap_w
params.rationale: mm, a 10 mm hook-and-loop battery strap.

params.name: strap_bay_w
params.rationale: mm between the strap slots' inner edges: the widest pack the strap straddles (LAVA II 480 is 15.5 wide), so the 320 and the 480 both fit.

params.name: strap_slot_w
params.rationale: mm, slot across the strap's thickness: 1.5 strap + print shrink + fumbling.

params.name: motor_base_d
params.rationale: mm, the 1102's stator mount/base (listing: '11 mm', the stator size).

params.name: motor_base_h
params.rationale: mm, base height below the bell. Envelope (A3).

params.name: shaft_d
params.rationale: mm, 1102 shaft (listing).

params.name: shaft_exposed

params.name: lead_d
params.rationale: mm, a motor lead's 3 x 30 AWG wires bundled.

params.name: prop_pitch_deg
params.rationale: GF 1811 3-blade, drawn: hub, three flat pitched blades. Shape for the view; the clearance it is checked for is its swept disc and the blade corners.

params.name: fc_hole_d
params.rationale: mm, the AIO's mounting holes (M1.4 clearance). Assumed.

params.name: socket_h
params.rationale: mm, a JST 1.25 3-pin motor socket on the AIO's top face, at the edge facing its motor. Position assumed; P4 checks the board that arrives.

params.name: screw_head_h
params.rationale: mm, M1.4 pan-head screws.

params.name: bt20_h
params.rationale: mm, one half of a BT2.0 plug pair.

params.name: bed_x_mm
params.rationale: mm, Snapmaker U1 build plate X (user: 270 mm bed).

params.name: bed_y_mm
params.rationale: mm, Snapmaker U1 build plate Y.

params.name: bed_z_mm
params.rationale: Snapmaker U1 build volume (user: 270 mm bed).

params.name: brim_mm
params.rationale: mm of brim per side: the duct rims touch the bed on a 1.3 mm wall; a brim keeps them down and is snipped off.

params.name: nozzle_d_mm
params.rationale: mm, the U1's stock nozzle.

params.name: extrusion_width_mm
params.rationale: mm, 1.05 x nozzle - a stock profile's line width; 3 of them is the wall rule.

params.name: layer_height_mm
params.rationale: mm, 0.2: half the nozzle, the PETG default; plate_t and hub_t are whole layers.

params.name: perimeters
params.rationale: Wall loops. Every thin wall here is designed as exactly 3 of them.

params.name: infill_fraction
params.rationale: Thin walls everywhere: there is no room for infill; treat as solid.

params.name: print_speed_mm_s
params.rationale: mm/s nominal; an ordinary PETG speed (the estimate derates it).

params.name: max_print_time_h
params.rationale: An afternoon with a 10-year-old: a print that runs overnight is a print he does not see.

params.name: max_filament_g
params.rationale: g, one spool: the frame uses ~2% of it.

params.name: duct_thrust_factor
params.rationale: Static thrust with the duct relative to the open-prop test. Tight ducts can add 10-20%; a printed duct with a 1 mm gap and no shaped lip is assumed to cost 10% instead. ASSUMPTION (A1).

params.name: hover_eff_g_per_w
params.rationale: g of thrust per electrical watt at hover. ASSUMPTION (A2): typical of 0802 class motors on 40 mm props; refine from a blackbox log of a real hover.

params.name: usable_capacity_frac
params.rationale: Land at ~3.5 V/cell: 80% of rated capacity, kinder to cheap 1S packs.

params.name: plate_layout
params.rationale: 'arms' = the hand-drawn first layout (hub-to-motor arms, 3 flat spokes); 'spoked' = the layout the topology optimiser found (see geometry.members and tools/run_topopt.py). 'arms' lost: first mode ~160 Hz against C4's 200.

params.name: spoke_count
params.rationale: Spokes per motor seat. The optimiser drew 5; 5 lost: 0.6 g more for a thrust-to-weight of 3.025 - no margin on C1. 3 lost: crash stiffness 0.85-1.18x the hand-drawn frame's.

params.name: spoke_phase_deg
params.rationale: Angle of the first spoke from the seat-to-centre direction. 45 (spokes on the diagonals of the seat) lost nothing; 0 (one spoke straight at the hub, one straight out) gave the same mode and half the crash stiffness (1.0x vs 2.2x).

params.name: bridge_w
params.rationale: mm, flat flange under each hub-to-web bridge's rib. 6.0 lost: 0.1 g for 4 Hz of first mode.

params.name: topopt_h
params.rationale: mm, FE grid size. 0.5 halves the error and quadruples the run time.

params.name: topopt_rmin
params.rationale: mm, density-filter radius: the optimiser's length scale. 1.6 lost: with projection it drew members under 1 mm wide.

params.name: prop_block_mm
params.rationale: mm of equivalent depth charged per mm^2 of plate under a prop, on top of its mass: blocking downwash costs like 2 x plate_t of material. Replaced 'prop_area_cost = 3' (a multiplier on mass), which starved every spoke.

params.name: bounce_g
params.rationale: g of vertical acceleration on the fixed masses for the bending load case. The problem is linear, so the value only scales compliance; 1 g keeps it readable.

params.name: crash_load_n
params.rationale: N, a hit on a duct rim (in-plane). ~ the quad at 4 m/s stopping in ~10 ms.

params.name: topopt_w_thrust
params.rationale: Objective weight on bounce stiffness (the vibration mode); see topopt_w_crash.

params.name: topopt_w_crash
params.rationale: Objective weights: bounce stiffness (the vibration mode) vs. crash stiffness. 2:1 for bounce lost: mode 434 Hz but crash stiffness fell to 0.31x the hand-drawn frame's, and a 10-year-old's drone is mostly a crash-test article.

params.name: topopt_iters
params.rationale: Optimiser iterations: 20 per projection-sharpness step (beta 1..16), then until it stops moving.

params.name: topopt_member_h
params.rationale: mm, height of an optimised member: plate_t + rib_h, the baseline rib's height, so the two layouts are compared at the same depth. A flat 1.8 mm optimised plate lost: bending stiffness goes as depth cubed, and the first run's flat layout bounced at 116 Hz against the ribbed baseline's 217.

params.name: member_clear
params.rationale: mm a deep member keeps from the motor's base and from the AIO footprint, where the plate stays plate_t thin (motor seat; strap path under the board).

params.name: topopt_mass_frac
params.rationale: Optimised plate mass as a fraction of the baseline plate's.

params.name: topopt_smooth
params.rationale: mm, corner rounding on the extracted outline; also deletes slivers < 0.8 mm.

params.name: prop_sweep_half_h
params.rationale: mm, half-height of the band the prop occupies, for the clearance check.

asserted.hint: accepted provisionally, with a reason and an owner — an assumption, or a claim carried outside an evaluator's operating context — unresolved

blocked.hint: an evaluator skipped — its tool is missing here, it skipped itself on its input, or a prerequisite is not established — and none failed: no usable verdict

errored.hint: an evaluator errored: it crashed, so nothing was evaluated, and the evaluator itself is broken

fail.hint: an evaluator failed the current candidate, a physical result failed, or an evaluator's value does not meet the claim's acceptance condition

pass.hint: every evaluator is qualified and passed on the current inputs, inside its operating context, and every value compared with the acceptance condition meets it — checked does not mean true

pending.hint: an evaluator of the claim is unrun on the current inputs

refuted.hint: an evaluator failed the current candidate, a physical result failed, or an evaluator's value does not meet the claim's acceptance condition

stale.hint: a pass whose read set has changed since, or whose prerequisite is invalidated or unrun: nothing is checked now

unclaimed.hint: no evaluator, none qualified, one unqualified, or one outside its operating context; or an assumption nobody owns

unverified.hint: waits on an article: no physical result yet, or a pass no article binds to the current inputs

verified.hint: every evaluator is qualified and passed on the current inputs, inside its operating context, and every value compared with the acceptance condition meets it — checked does not mean true
